text.p: Bonds nosed higher, closing the spread with the Bund after underperforming on Tuesday, as the market waited to see whether the Bank of Portugal cut interest rates later on Wednesday.
Few analysts expected the Bank to make any adjustment in its 6.0 percent repo rate or its 5.7 percent drain rate although it would not be the first time that it has sprung a surprise.
Traders were also waiting for economic data from the U.S. on non-durable goods and house sales.
"The longer end will probably see only light trade until the U.S. figures are released. They could consolidate around 65 basis points from the Bunds," said one trader.
The first U.S. figures are due at 1230 GMT.

If the Bank of Portugal surprised the market and cut rates 25 basis points, this could provoke a five basis point steepening in the curve, traders said. But it would not have much impact on the longer end.
The spread between the two- and 10-year bonds stood at 115 basis points against 113 on Tuesday.
